headline: Actor Don placed on 5-day remand in Salman Shah murder case
summary: A Dhaka court has granted a five-day remand for actor Ashraful Haque alias Don, who was arrested in connection with the murder case of popular film star Salman Shah. This development comes nearly three decades after Shah's death.
details: A Dhaka court has granted a five-day remand for actor Ashraful Haque alias Don, who was arrested in connection with the murder case of popular film star Salman Shah. Metropolitan Magistrate Jewel Rana issued the order on Thursday after a hearing.

The investigating officer, Inspector Mujibur Rahman of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) Dhaka Metropolitan South, had applied for a seven-day remand for Don on August 20. The court had set today for the hearing in the presence of the accused.

During the hearing, the investigating officer told the court that Don's remand was necessary for the investigation of this sensational case. State counsel Omar Faruk Faruki emphasized the gravity of the case, stating that the public awaits justice.
The prosecution also alleged that the defense had attempted to obstruct the case and issued threats. They argued that a fair investigation requires the accused to be remanded.

Don's lawyer, Faridul Islam, argued that his client would have left the country much earlier if he were involved, proving his innocence. He contended that there was no need for Don to be remanded in this case.
Don was arrested on August 9 at Dhaka's Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport and subsequently sent to jail. His bail application was rejected by the court on August 12.

Salman Shah's body was recovered from his Eskaton residence in Dhaka on September 6, 1996. Last year, nearly 29 years after his death, a court ordered a murder case to be filed in connection with the incident.

Salman Shah's mother, Nila Chowdhury, through her brother Alamgir Kumkum, filed the murder case at Ramna Police Station last October. The case names 11 individuals, including Salman Shah's former wife Samira Haque and actor Ashraful Haque alias Don. The CID is currently investigating the case, with the next investigation report due on August 30.

headline_marked: [[Nearly 1,500 missing]] after Nepal-Tibet floods kill over 177, China reports 100 nationals missing
headline: Nearly 1,500 missing after Nepal-Tibet floods kill over 177, China reports 100 nationals missing
summary: Massive flash floods and mudslides, triggered by a glacial collapse, have devastated areas along the Nepal-Tibet border, leaving a trail of destruction and over 177 confirmed deaths with nearly 1,500 people missing.
details: Catastrophic flash floods and mudslides have swept across regions along the Nepal-Tibet border, resulting in at least 177 confirmed deaths and leaving nearly 1,500 people unaccounted for. The disaster has caused widespread devastation, submerging villages and infrastructure.

The United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that the floods were caused by a glacial collapse, which also triggered seismic activity in the affected areas. This sudden natural event led to rivers overflowing their banks and massive mudslides.

Among the missing are nearly 100 Chinese nationals, including tourists, pilgrims, and other personnel, as confirmed by China's foreign ministry. Nepal has also reported 468 tourists, primarily foreigners, out of contact.

Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with authorities from both Nepal and China coordinating efforts. China is in close communication with Nepal and has been informing relevant embassies about the situation of missing foreigners.
Bangladesh has offered its support to flood-hit Nepal, though the Bangladeshi embassy has confirmed that no Bangladeshi casualties have been reported in the landslides or floods.
caption:
Over 1,700 people are dead or missing following catastrophic floods and mudslides along the Nepal-Tibet border. The disaster was reportedly triggered by a glacial collapse.

Catastrophic flash floods and mudslides have swept across regions along the Nepal-Tibet border, resulting in at least 177 confirmed deaths and leaving nearly 1,500 people unaccounted for. The disaster has caused widespread devastation, submerging villages and infrastructure.

The United States Geological Survey (USGS) reported that the floods were caused by a glacial collapse, which also triggered seismic activity in the affected areas. This sudden natural event led to rivers overflowing their banks and massive mudslides.

Among the missing are nearly 100 Chinese nationals, including tourists, pilgrims, and other personnel, as confirmed by China's foreign ministry. Nepal has also reported 468 tourists, primarily foreigners, out of contact.

Search and rescue operations are ongoing, with authorities from both Nepal and China coordinating efforts. China is in close communication with Nepal and has been informing relevant embassies about the situation of missing foreigners.

Bangladesh has offered its support to flood-hit Nepal, though the Bangladeshi embassy has confirmed that no Bangladeshi casualties have been reported in the landslides or floods.
